WoW: Forever

Retribution Paladin

Two-handed melee with Holy magic layered on top. Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 12 as Holy damage. at level 6 turns it from auto-attack-and-wait into something you actually play, twenty levels earlier than Classic gave a Paladin a button.

WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated October 8, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70245 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Retribution build has been tested.

A widely-published level-30 Retribution build spends two points on CrusadeCrusadeTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage dealt by 2%. Increased by an additional 2% against Demon and Undead targets., and nobody can tell you whether the tree still offers it. No Blizzard note mentions it leaving in the September 24 build (1.60.1.70009), the beta's first balance pass, and build 1.60.1.70245 has not deleted the talent. But the client cannot tell you which talents a Forever tree can reach. It also omits Champion of the LightChampion of the LightTalentCastInstantIncreases your spell damage by up to 100% of your Intellect. and Sacred ArbiterSacred ArbiterTalentCastInstantIncreases the damage of your Holy Strike ability by 20% and causes it to refresh all Judgement effects on the target., which are both unquestionably live. Check in game whether you can spend a point in CrusadeCrusadeTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage dealt by 2%. Increased by an additional 2% against Demon and Undead targets., and treat those two points as the least reliable part of that build.

Wowhead reports that beta testers and class discords currently consider Retribution the single most overtuned spec in the level-20 bracket, and expects changes. The level-30 cap opened on October 1, and that same build cut Champion of the LightChampion of the LightTalentCastInstantIncreases your spell damage by up to 100% of your Intellect.. Treat the talent and gearing advice below as a snapshot rather than a settled answer.

What Retribution is for

Layering Holy damage onto a two-handed swing, with a real button to press from level 6. Seal of CommandSeal of CommandLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost65 ManaDuration30 secGives the Paladin a chance to deal additional Holy damage equal to 70% of normal weapon damage. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Lasts 30 sec. Unleashing this Seal's energy will judge an enemy, instantly causing 48.5 Holy damage, 97 if the target is stunned or incapacitated. at 20 procs Holy damage scaled off the swing, and a stun amplifies its Judgement.

Wowhead's overtuning warning is the only published comment aimed squarely at this spec. It is not a levelling score: no source publishes one for any Paladin spec, and a score would only measure solo kill speed.

You have no area damage until ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. at 20. Pull one target at a time. Paladin has no movement tools either; the published guides call it "slow, very slow."

Treat mana as an extension of your health bar. Topping up with Holy LightHoly LightLevel 1 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 9Cast2.5 sec castCost35 ManaRange40 yd rangeHeals a friendly target for 43. and killing the next thing at low mana usually beats sitting down to drink.

Multi-target: none until 20. Then ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec., and it is expensive. Blizzard publishes no target cap for it. The patchy damage beyond the first few targets was a bug, and the September 24 build fixed Consecration's failure to apply its increased damage effect to some targets, along with its inconsistent Z axis.

Later, Sacred ArbiterSacred ArbiterTalentCastInstantIncreases the damage of your Holy Strike ability by 20% and causes it to refresh all Judgement effects on the target. gives Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 12 as Holy damage. +20% damage and makes it refresh all Judgement debuffs, so staying in melee maintains them without re-judging.

Stat priority

Weapon DPS, then Hit and Expertise, critical strike, Spell Power, Strength, Intellect, Agility, Stamina.

Hit and Expertise barely appear on gear at this level, so they are close to irrelevant below 30. A slower weapon makes Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 12 as Holy damage. hit harder, but raw weapon DPS usually wins.

Intellect matters much more from 26 points in the tree, at level 35. There Champion of the LightChampion of the LightTalentCastInstantIncreases your spell damage by up to 100% of your Intellect. begins converting it into spell damage: 20% per point spent, up to 60% at max rank. The October 1 build cut that from 33% per point, or 100% at max. Wowhead, Icy Veins and ClassicWoW.gg may still print the old figure, and so does the client: build 1.60.1.70245 still reads 100% of Intellect. Blizzard's note is the one to believe.

Blizzard also removed a tooltip line that claimed the talent increased Healing too. It never did, so treat this as spell damage only.

Published gear lists split into a Spell Power build and an Attack Power build, and call both competitive at level 20.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
